To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) unstable low current discharges can transform into stable discharges in the presence of wind and rain.

1) The transition from unstable to stable discharges occurs at a current of about 0.5 to 1 mA; 2) Stable dry-band discharges can be formed under the influence of artificial rain and wind, even at currents below 1 mA; and 3) The energy density per cycle increases during unstable to stable transitions, and during discharge shortening.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the stability of discharges and their effect on the ageing of outdoor insulation.
the electrical characteristics of discharges in the range of 0.1 to 10 mA, with the aim of improving understanding of the processes involved in discharge stabilization and compression.
the processes of discharge formation and growth on polymeric insulators under wet weather conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the energy transfer from the discharge to the surface is a key mechanism in the ageing process, and is strongly dependent upon the nature of the discharge.

the discharge characteristics of a surface discharge on a wet surface are a complex function of current, wind and rain, and that the energy transferred to the surface during the discharge is a significant factor in the ageing process.
low current discharges are a significant cause of surface ageing on polymeric insulators, and that the nature of the discharge is strongly dependent on the prevailing weather conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the discharge characteristics and energy density per cycle are the two important parameters for predicting the lifetime of insulators.
low current surface dischargers are not necessarily benign.
surface discharges on polymeric insulation in the presence of wind and rain may not be the simple process that has been assumed in the past.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the discharge characteristics change significantly when the discharge current is in the range 0.5-1.5 mA, and that the discharge characteristics are strongly dependent on the environmental conditions.

the energy density in surface discharges is a key parameter in understanding the ageing of insulating materials, and that this parameter should be used in the development of predictive models for insulator ageing.
the electrical characteristics of surface discharges can change significantly in the presence of wind and rain.
